quotes.text: Digital debt is the massive accumulation of unverified and unmanaged digital artifacts that eventually overwhelm your human cognitive capacity to make sense of them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a crisp definition of the episode's central concept.

quotes.text: Because in reality, your AI isn't saving you time. It's just moving the work from the creation phase to the validation phase, and that second phase is much more expensive for your business.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes AI productivity claims as a shift of effort into costly validation.

quotes.text: It doesn't matter how fast the AI can type. What matters is how fast your leadership can act on what the AI produced.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core idea behind decision velocity as a success metric.

quotes.text: Every flow created with AI assistance should be required to have a human co-owner and a written statement that describes exactly what the flow does in plain English.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete governance rule against orphaned AI-built automations.

quotes.text: The hard truth is that co-pilot doesn't just accelerate your work, it accelerates entropy. A clean, shiny dashboard that hides a rotting internal process isn't an asset, it's a ticking time bomb.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable summary warning of the episode's thesis.

takeaways: More Copilot output does not mean more productivity when every artifact still needs human validation; unverified content piles up as digital debt.
Teams chats, Loop components and AI-built Power Automate flows compound that debt through fragmented context, ownerless decisions and silent breakage.
Measure decision velocity instead of time saved, and pay down the debt with kill-switch governance, weekly health checks and a 30/60/90-day plan.
hook: Your Copilot rollout is producing three times more content, but nobody trusts it. This episode is for leaders and Microsoft 365 architects who want to see how unverified AI output turns into digital debt, and how to measure and govern for trusted decisions instead of volume.
